params.body:
The review gate judges the sources a piece **cites**. It says nothing about the
sentences. Until now a body written by the assistant went model → editor →
client without one deterministic check, while `suggest.mjs` next door had been
writing insights in ProveML against the fact store for a week. The body was the
last place in the chain where a claim reached a client unopposed, and the worst
place for it, because the body is the part the client actually reads.

`packages/pipeline/article-writer.mjs`:

- `writerStoreFor(article)` — the facts of the sources this piece cites, under
  the key shape the bridge already uses.
- `writerInstructionsFor(article)` — generated with `promptFor`, never a
  hand-written field list.
- `gateBody(text, article)` — verify, strip, and one verdict.
- `draftWithProof(...)` — write, gate, one retry with the verifier's errors as
  the feedback, kept only if it verifies at least as well as the first.

Wired into `/articles/assist/draft` (mode `draft` only: a rewrite keeps the
meaning of a passage the editor already has, and angles are headlines) and
`/articles/:id/draft-full`. The verdict travels with the draft; the Studio shows
it (Trendwolves/gentells-studio).

**The one judgement worth arguing with: not strict.** Strict makes every figure
outside a claim an error, which is right for four short insight fields where
nearly every number is a claim about the store, and wrong for a 600-word body
full of ordinary editorial numbers. Failing those would send the retry out to
rewrite sound prose and hand the editor a verdict that reads as failure on a
piece with nothing wrong in it. So the two questions are asked separately:
claims the store contradicts gate the retry, figures no claim covers are counted
and shown. Nothing is hidden either way, which is what strict was protecting.

The verdict is never written to the piece. It describes the text the model just
returned and the editor is expected to rewrite it; what survives an edit is the
citation review, keyed to the evidence itself.

Seven new tests on the part no model is in: which facts a writer may reach for
(a stronger uncited pattern in the same table stays out of the store), a wrong
number failing with the field named, no markup counting as a refusal and not a
pass, a figure outside every claim counted and not gated. The model call is not
tested: a test that fakes a writer copies the writer and proves nothing.

Full suite: 694 of 694.
params.title: Proof in the writing, not only in the apparatus
